entry.title: Paper Mario The Thousand Year Door v0.14.1
entry.content:
## Bug Fixes
- Fixed a crash when receiving items from players whose names contain `<` or `>`. - Fixed duplicate badges and consumables on the first shop purchase when Remote Items is enabled. - Fixed the Crystal Stars goal interrupting pickup animations, including chest pickups. - Fixed the Chapter 2 Shadow Sirens event causing item pickups to softlock. - Fixed invisible falling Dull Bones in `gon_03` caused by overworld enemy replacement. - Fixed randomized Piders remaining near the ceiling, using incorrect descent distances, and only detecting Mario from one side. - Fixed Monochrome Clefts, including an encounter in `win_00`, being missed by overworld enemy replacement. - Fixed tossing a coconut during the full-inventory prompt removing the protected coconut from key items. - Fixed generation failures involving the Crystal Stars goal, All Star Shuffle, and self-locking plando in another slot. - Fixed reversed controls while riding Yoshi in Mirror Mode. - Fixed Doopliss appearing from the wrong side during his post-defeat moon entrance in `gra_00` when Mirror Mode is enabled. - Fixed a memory leak during Great Tree room transitions.
## Boss randomizer adjustments
- Improved Golden Fuzzy, Hooktail, and Gloomtail cutscene framing and replacement positioning. - Corrected Gloomtail’s speech-bubble placement and camera obstruction after the partner cutaway. - Removed Gloomtail’s dragon roar when replaced by a non-dragon enemy. - Corrected paper-model facing for replacements such as tutorial Crump and the Doopliss rematch. - Shortened the Doopliss rematch’s pre-battle scene when randomized by removing partner dialogue. - Permanently disabled Vivian’s mid-battle return in the Doopliss rematch. - Removed Goombella’s tutorial appearance and dialogue from tutorial Crump’s battle.
## Other changes
- Removed the Shuffle Chapter Stats option.

entry.title: Freedom Planet 2 v1.0.0r2
entry.content:
Changes since Prerelease 1:
**FIXES**
- Items with multiple classifications are now properly coloured in the text chat and display the most relevant sprite type. (Initially became a problem with Perfect Dark, which has a lot of items tagged as both Progression and Useful). - Hopefully finally stomped out the issue where modded items caused the end of the shops to fall apart. - Fixed the Spam Trap getting stuck when changing scenes. - RingLink had some weirdness regarding activating when it shouldn't that should be fixed at this point.
**ADDITIONS**
- Added a config option for whether or not Fists of Frogs should send hints out. - Silly little config option for the shop vendor names. - A, S and Rainbow S-Rank locations. - Merga Goal option. - Wordle and Flood Traps. - Stupid joke config option that makes various bits of text behave like they do in Super Mario 64 (which has missing characters be replaced by the previous one). - Games without a DeathLink message now display jokes/references rather than just "DeathLink received from [PLAYER]".
**ADJUSTMENTS**
- Changed the stage edits made to Sky Bridge. - Spike Ball Trap now specifically spawns on the screen edges rather than a fixed distance from the player.
**KNOWN ISSUES**
- The Trivia Trap still can't kill the BFF2000 or Bakunawa Chase Airship properly. - Swap Traps can still sometimes leave a lingering hitbox on the player. - Fists of Frog's hint sending is still really picky. - The Remote Player handler still seems to freeze the game upon close if active, requiring it to be force killed (still thinking about just throwing that out to be honest). - Game still seems to crash a lot, seemingly at random. The randomness paired with the fact that I can't strap a debugger to it makes diagnosing these a pain.

entry.title: Slay the Spire II v1.2.0
entry.content:
> [!WARNING] > Both Slay the Spire II and this Archipelago Mod are in active development. As such, while this _is_ playable, expect there to be bugs and limited features. We appreciate your playtesting! ## Setup For installation, YAML configuration, generation and connection instructions, see [the Slay the Spire II setup guide](https://github.com/dlueben1/Slay-the-Spire-2-Archipelago/blob/setup-docs-do-not-delete/world/spire2/docs/setup_en.md). Archipelago **Launcher v0.6.7+** is required for generation. Install **STS2-RitsuLib 0.6.0+** separately. # Version Information - **Archipelago Client:** 2.0.0 - **APWorld:** 1.2.0 - **Slay the Spire II main branch:** v0.107.1 - **Slay the Spire II beta branch:** v0.111.0 # Changelist ## Major changes ### Multiplayer You can now play Archipelago in co-op! Connect using your own AP slot and YAML, or join as a guest without an AP slot. The host needs an AP connection. This required @Terairk to rewrite the mod side code as StS2 does multiplayer in a very specific deterministic way which meant rewriting everything. Some behaviour may or may not be intentionally changed from previous mod versions to allow multiplayer to even exist. Future updates will take longer as multiplayer is very complicated and some future updates may or may not work on multiplayer. Most of your favourite singleplayer features are supported, with a few exceptions: - **AP menu rewards can only be claimed outside combat, including potions.** This is a limitation of how Slay the Spire 2 handles multiplayer rewards. Working around it would require substantial changes and is not planned for the foreseeable future. You cannot stockpile unclaimed AP potion rewards and withdraw them during the Act 3 boss fight—claim the potions you want before entering combat. - **DeathLink is supported, but Death Fragments are disabled in multiplayer due to state divergences.** - **Anytime Ancient rewards are recommended for multiplayer.** In Start of Act mode, Ancient rewards missed before a checkpoint cannot be claimed later in that run. ### Traps Added **nine trap types** for singleplayer and multiplayer: Weak, Frail, Vulnerable, No Draw, Tangled, Vakuu, Confused, Sloth, and Dazed. Future traps may or may not work in multiplayer due to state divergences or balance concerns in multiplayer. Traps are **disabled by default**. Set **`trap_chance`** to give filler items a chance of being replaced by a trap, then adjust each trap's weight to choose which ones can appear and how often. Received traps wait for combat, with **at most one trap activating per player turn**. They have their own queue, so receiving a trap does not use up your combat buff allowance. ### Filler and combat buff rework Combat buffs now activate **at most once per player per combat**, in both singleplayer and multiplayer. Extra buffs stay queued for later combats instead of all being consumed at once. This is to handle the weird case where you log into the game again (like if you took a break or juggling multiplayer games) only for 20 buffs to be consumed and also prevents the bad handling where some buffs were unable to be stacked properly. Strength, Dexterity, and Artifact buffs now grant **1 instead of 2**, and Plating grants **4 instead of 5**. Vigor, Thorns, Friendship, and permanent deck effects keep their existing strengths. The idea is that buffs should only be worth roughly 1 relic of help and shouldn't boost the player too much otherwise they can go out of logic even easier than it already is. ### More flexible randomization Added the YAML option **`use_new_logic`**, enabled by default. The new logic considers your overall strength more flexibly. For example, extra cards and relics can let you progress where the old logic would require another Progressive Rest. This approach applies across more of your upgrades, allowing greater variety in which items arrive early and which combinations let you advance. Basically allows more randomness and variety. May or may not be harder than the old logic. ### Better saves and checkpoints - Choose from **nine singleplayer checkpoint positions per character**, including new pre-boss campfire checkpoints in all three acts. - Manage multiple multiplayer campaigns, with separate **Floor Recovery** and **AP Checkpoint** loading options. - Singleplayer checkpoints are stored locally by default. **AP Server Cloud Saves** remain available as an optional setting, disabled by default, so you can keep remote backups without every player automatically adding large saves to the AP server’s storage. ### Version compatibility **Development and gameplay testing have been on beta `0.111.0`.** A build for main `0.107.1` is included, but if you encounter problems there, please switch to `0.111.0`. Existing YAMLs do not need the new per-character starter fields: omitted settings inherit their global settings. Use the updated APWorld and client for **traps and per-character progressive starter overrides**. Older clients do not support the new trap items, and older APWorlds reject the new per-character starter fields when they are explicitly included in a YAML. New predefined-character aliases and expanded rosters also require the updated APWorld. ---
Full details ### Saves and checkpoints - The singleplayer checkpoint picker lets you start a new run or load a previously reached checkpoint. - Checkpoints cover the initial Ancient, each act’s treasure room and pre-boss campfire, and the defeated Act 1 and Act 2 bosses. - Starting a new run preserves existing checkpoints until you reach and overwrite their corresponding positions. - AP checkpoints are stored separately for each slot and character, independently of ordinary game saves. - Enabling **AP Server Cloud Saves** backs up the latest eligible singleplayer checkpoint for each character and enables **Load Remote Save**. - The multiplayer campaign picker includes campaign history, archiving, abandonment, and deletion controls. - Added **Local Save Management** settings for deleting AP singleplayer checkpoints or multiplayer campaigns. ### Logic and generation - Set **`use_new_logic: false`** in your YAML to use the previous logic. - New logic allows base-game characters to progress without their starter card or relic when other rewards provide enough support. - **Start of Act** mode still requires the corresponding Ancient unlocks for later acts. - When floor, gold, and potion checks are all disabled, generation automatically uses old logic to reduce generation failures. - Improved early item placement for configurations with fewer checks. - Fixed an Act 3 shop-access logic issue. - Rare Card Rewards receive normal progression placement priority. - Elite and Boss Gold are treated as useful rewards rather than required progression when new logic is active and Shop Sanity is disabled. ### Traps and filler rewards - **`trap_chance`** ranges from 0–100 and defaults to 0. It controls the chance of replacing a filler item, without adding extra items or checks. - Each trap has a **None / Low / Medium / High** weight. None excludes that trap; enabling traps with every trap weight set to None produces a clear configuration error. - Weak, Frail, and Vulnerable apply one turn of their respective debuff. No Draw blocks extra draws, and Tangled increases Attack costs by 1 for the turn. - Vakuu plays your hand on one additional turn, no earlier than turn two, without Whispering Earring's energy bonus. - Confused randomizes drawn card costs for the rest of combat. Sloth applies a six-card limit per turn for the rest of combat. Dazed shuffles two Dazed into your combat draw pile. - Traps use the game's normal effects and interactions, including Artifact protection where applicable. - Filler weights now use direct per-item values: **None = 0, Low = 1, Medium = 3, High = 5**. - Combat buffs are universal; One Gold and Five Gold remain character-specific rewards. - Multiplayer buff and trap queues restore their delivery history when reconnecting or loading a campaign, preserving pending effects without replaying effects already consumed. ### Cards, relics, and rewards - Fixed **Additional Card Reward** doing nothing. It grants an actual extra three-card reward after combat in both singleplayer and multiplayer. - Fixed **Splash** having its cross-character attack choices restricted by AP character locks. - Cross-character effects, including **Kaleidoscope**, use the appropriate player’s card pools in multiplayer. Built-in character pools remain available, while modded character pools follow that player’s configured roster. - Multiplayer supports progressive starters, Ascension changes, combat buffs, and post-combat card upgrade/removal effects. - Received rewards and progression are preserved when reconnecting or loading a multiplayer campaign. ### Modded characters - **Downfall:** cross-character card pools now preserve Downfall's Prismatic Gem restrictions after Archipelago applies its configured character pools. - **IntoTheSpireverse:** shared character buttons and alternate arrows remain usable when the AP roster includes alternate characters, including rosters that omit their base-game counterparts. Selection follows the configured roster and AP character unlocks. - **Colourful Philosophers:** alternate characters sharing a base character's energy colour now display their character name, making their card pools easier to distinguish. - Added optional **`progressive_starter_card`** and **`progressive_starter_relic`** overrides for each character in Advanced Characters. Explicit true/false values override the global setting for that character; leaving a field out inherits the global setting. Both still require **Include Floor Checks**. - Per-character starter settings apply to item generation, logic, and starter upgrades in singleplayer and multiplayer, including modded characters that support the game's starter upgrade behaviour. - Added some specific handling for popular modded characters so you can add them to your yaml easier. Namely Watcher from Lamali, IntoTheSpireverse and "Downfall - Classic" characters. - Added better naming when using a 'Pre-defined modded character' such as those from the above mods so they say 'Watcher Floor 5' instead of 'Custom Character 4 Floor 5' - Allow up to 20 modded characters (up from 5 - usual modded character caveats apply), for up to 25 characters including the vanilla roster. ### YAML builder website - Added trap chance and individual trap weights under **Checks & Rewards**. - Added the new logic toggle under **Progression**. - Added per-character progressive starter card and relic controls under **Character Setup**, alongside Ascension configuration. Each can use the global setting or explicitly enable/disable it for that character. - The builder exports per-character starter fields only when an override is selected, keeping default exports free of these new fields. Starter overrides are inactive when floor checks are disabled. - Support for up to 20 modded characters, with easier entry of custom character IDs. - Generated YAMLs now include `requires` with Archipelago Launcher **0.6.7** and APWorld **1.2.0** as minimum versions, matching the template YAML. APWorld requirements use the major/minor version, so patch releases do not raise the YAML requirement. - The template YAML now includes explanations of option values and the available item options. ### Settings and interface - Added client-side overrides for **Ancient Mode** and **Ancient Pool**, allowing you to choose different Ancient settings for a new run without regenerating the multiworld. - Ancient overrides apply to new runs, including multiplayer. Continuing a saved run preserves its original settings. - Added clearer singleplayer and multiplayer entry points on the main menu. - You can disconnect and change AP slots from the main menu without restarting the game. - Improved the Ascension display to show the actual active Ascensions, including nonconsecutive combinations. - Fixed the top bar showing two bosses when AP Double Boss is inactive, in both singleplayer and multiplayer even when Ascension 10 is disabled. Boss icons and tooltips now reflect whether the second boss is enabled. - Fixed Ascension UI briefly showing Ascension 10 when starting an AP run. Multiplayer lobby displays now follow the host's AP Ascension settings. - Fixed rendering issues with the progressive campfire status icons. - Improved Universal Tracker explanations and check ordering, keeping numbered checks in a more natural order. - Added **Export Bug Report** under Archipelago Settings, with an equivalent `ap report` console command, to package multiplayer divergence reports and game logs for sharing. ### Compatibility and fixes - Fixed an IntentGraph interaction that could keep enemies at higher-Ascension damage after AP disabled Deadly Enemies. Ascension-dependent graph labels now follow AP's Deadly Enemies setting. This was a bug that only existed on the multiplayer beta branches for some unknown reasons but didn't affect the previous main release. - Restored **Python 3.11 compatibility** for the APWorld by using `typing_extensions.override` instead of the Python 3.12+ only `typing.override`. - One client package contains separate main and beta builds, with the appropriate build selected automatically. - Reduced unnecessary APWorld compatibility warnings for patch-version differences. - Fixed connection handling for missing or null slot-data values, including a case that could interrupt an otherwise successful login. - Improved APWorld slot-data compatibility and Universal Tracker restoration. - Missing or incorrectly configured modded characters produce a clear connection error instead of silently substituting their checks. - Added clearer validation for invalid character configurations. - Extensive internal cleanup and automated checks make it easier to maintain main/beta compatibility going forward.
## Known Issues/Limitations - Beta **0.111.0** is the recommended game branch and has received the most development and gameplay testing. Main **0.107.1** is included but has limited or no gameplay testing. - In multiplayer, AP menu rewards can only be claimed outside combat; Death Fragments are disabled. **Anytime** Ancient rewards are recommended. - All modded characters configured in your seed must be installed and enabled when connecting. - Older APWorlds may require a compatibility confirmation with this client. Use the updated APWorld and client together for the new traps, character aliases, expanded roster, and per-character starter settings.

entry.title: Rimworld v1.0.0.post0
entry.content:
### Features
More raid/negative filler variety - "raid traps" should now choose any "big threat," so can include things like infestations, mech drops, or animal insanity. Normal negative filler also has a chance for any negative event, including diseases and the like. Trade locations now have fake logic, so they aren't all in-logic at once. Quest locations have been added. Like raids and trade locations, completing a quest with an item for a reward will include a quest location item. Implemented deathlink - If a player on the server dies, it will cause a negative, stacking thought in all colonists. If a colonist dies, it will send a deathlink to the server.
### Bugfixes
Changed raid/trade locations so they can't be savescummed. Items sent as filler will now be sent in increments of ~200 silver, rather than (roughly) "1 full stack" Changed drop pod behavior to use the trading drop pod logic, so they drop closer to your base Location items can be stockpiled Blood Rain research should now grant correctly when sent from AP Fixed a bug where logic for raid/trade locations wasn't applying properly

entry.title: Ys Origin v2.1.1
entry.content:
A patch release: the 3F barrier fix from a Hugo player's report, and a logic audit against the game's room scripts. Requires **Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer**.
> **Take all three files, and take them together.** Seeds generated with 2.1.0 stay playable with the new dll.
## 🛠️ Mod fix
- **The 3F Transfer Room now always sends you to 4F first.** Its barrier teleports Yunica and Hugo to 4F unless the Blue Necklace is worn, and that teleport is the only way into the 4F rooms. A seed can hand you the necklace early, and walking in wearing it broke the barrier for good, so 4F was out of reach. Until you have been to 4F, the barrier now ignores the necklace. - **Saves already stuck this way are repaired.** If you broke the barrier before ever reaching 4F, it comes back the next time you are in a room next to it. Walk into it to be teleported to 4F, then come back with the necklace on to break it again.
## 🗺️ Logic
Ten places where the logic counted on a check or a passage the game blocks, found by checking every room against its scripts: - six room gates, including the 6F room (wind in, dash out), the 8F dive and the 24F bridge's way back; - four story checks, including Yunica's Black Pearl, which now waits for her 19F event; - the 2F Gemma Room's two checks are Yunica's and Hugo's only (Toal cannot enter it).
## ⚠️ What was and was not played
- The barrier fix was loaded in the retail game and its check was exercised in memory for each case. The room itself was not played through. - The logic changes passed AP's integration check, 60 random seeds and 8 three-player seeds.
## 🐞 Known issues
- **Rado's Annex and story order** (from 2.1.0) is still not fixed in this dll. Hugo and Yunica can be turned around at the Rado Tower bridge by story flags from higher floors. - The known issues listed for 2.1.0 still apply.

entry.title: Spyro 2 v2.2.0
entry.content:
This release modifies both the Duckstation client (S2AP.Desktop.exe) and the APWorld (including the Bizhawk client). This release is not compatible with previous versions. As this release patches a significant DataStorage usage issue with the Duckstation client, full gemsanity players are urged to update immediately.
New Features: - Players can now menu out of Glimmer before entering Summer Forest for the first time. - Game overs prior to entering Summer Forest continue to redirect the player to Glimmer, as in vanilla.
Changes: - The minimum supported AP version is now 0.6.6, up from 0.6.1. - Most users will no longer need to run the Duckstation client in admin mode. This is no longer forced on opening it. - Gemsanity Rework - Gem locations and items are now separated. - The player may specify how many gems to become locations. - Gems will behave normally if only locations are added. - Adding 500 or more locations requires host approval. - Simplified gem item options. - When choosing gem bundles or full gemsanity, the player's gem location count may be overridden to provide enough locations. - If not logically required, red gems are now filler items. Otherwise, they are converted to green and blue gems. - This significantly improves the speed of generation and success rate for full gemsanity. - When Level Locks are on, beating Ripto unlocks Dragon Shores permanently. - The lock now only prevents entering from out of bounds. - The trick enabling wall access from Zephyr with Double Jump now also grants access to the two gems outside Metro Speedway into logic. (Coded by PhoenixAki)
Bug Fixes - [Duckstation] Fixed a critical bug where inefficient DataStorage use could cause issues up to and including crashes in full gemsanity seeds. - Fixed a logic error that incorrectly handled the warp from Crush to Autumn Plains when the player had swim but not climb. - [Bizhawk] Fixed a pair of bugs around Sparx range and the Lazy Sparx Trap. - Fixed a bug where loading into an in-progress gemsanity seed could release checks based on your vanilla progression instead of your AP progression. - [Duckstation] Fixed a bug where connecting before in game could cause filler items received offline to be lost. - Fixed a bug where Elora could let the player into the Ripto fight early under rare circumstances.

entry.title: Death's Door v0.4.2
entry.content:
# Death's Door Archipelago 0.4.2
Use apworld 0.4.2 together with mod 0.4.2. Seeds generated with apworld 0.4.0 or 0.4.1 also work with mod 0.4.2.
## Mod (ArchipelagoRandomizer 0.4.2)
### Skip Cutscenes - The late-game story scenes are now skipped, including on saves that are already under way: - the Grey Crow opening Death's Door - the Grey Crow and Death in the void - Death's talk after the Grey Crow fight - the crows' scene in the Hall of Doors - the Lord of Doors' speeches before the gauntlet and during the final fight - The camera pans that show what you just opened are now skipped too. These include the Castle Lockstone braziers, the Lost Cemetery ghosts, crow souls flying into an Ancient Door, and doors, levers and cleared fights. - The ending after the Lord of Doors and the credits still play. - The few cutscenes that can leave invisible walls behind are always skipped, whether or not Skip Cutscenes is on.
### Shop - With Shop Hints on, looking at a stat in the shop shows the item its next upgrade holds and hints it. - Progressive Strength, Dexterity, Haste and Magic now show the shop's stat icons, in white, in popups and in the Recent Items list.
### Door and stat tracker - While the game is paused, press Tab (keyboard) or Y (controller) to open a tracker panel. A small hint in the bottom-left of the pause menu shows this: - With entrance randomization, the doors of the area you're in and where each one leads once you've been through it. In coupled seeds the way back counts too. Page Up / Page Down or the triggers show other areas. - With Shop Upgrades on, the level you've received for each stat and how many of its upgrades you've bought. - The shop's description panel now shows your current level of each stat. The shop's bars only show what you bought.
### DeathLink - Fixed the game crashing when it received a DeathLink. - A DeathLink that arrives while you're rolling, invincible or just respawned is no longer lost. It kills you as soon as it can. - Fixed your own deaths sometimes not being sent after you received a DeathLink. - A DeathLink that arrives while you're already dead no longer kills you again after respawning. - The game now shows who caused a DeathLink when it kills you.
### Fixes - Fixed a possible crash when the connection to the server drops. - The Grove of Spirits Door check is now sent when you arrive in the Hall of Doors, even with Skip Cutscenes off. - Fixed short freezes when planting a Life Seed in a new pot. They happened even with planting checks off. - Fixed a freeze in entrance randomizer seeds when a door led to another door in the same area, such as one Hall of Doors door to another. - Fixed a bug in ItemChanger that logged an error every frame in some areas. This made log files grow to over 100 MB and could cause stutter.
## APWorld (deaths_door 0.4.2) - Every Life Seed now counts towards the logic. The tracker now shows the Green Tablet and the goal as reachable once you've planted enough seeds. - On the Universal Tracker map: - Planting pot pins follow each pot's own requirements. The Crypt pot needs Fire. - The Imp Loft pot pin has moved to the Ceramic Manor left wing. - The "Beat the Lord of Doors" and "Open the Green Ancient Tablet Door" pins only light up once you can actually do them. - Entrance randomizer never connects two Hall of Doors doors to each other. - Grunt's Old Mask is no longer shown as glitched in the tracker when you can actually get it. - Leaving Ceramic Manor through the gate to the Estate of the Urn Witch is now in logic. The gate opens from the inside, day or night. - Universal Tracker's `/get_logical_path <place>` now lists the doors to take from the Hall of Doors, in order, with where each one actually leads in your seed. It only uses doors you've been through and paths you can walk with your current items. - New option **Shop Hints** (on by default). It controls the shop preview and hints described above. - Corrected the descriptions of Extra Life Seeds and Planted Pots Required.
## README - The mod and apworld READMEs are now one README, attached to this release and included in the mod zip. It covers setup from start to finish, every in-game Mod Option and every yaml option, including the new shop and planting options.

APWorld remains **0.29.0**; the unchanged APWorld download is included for convenience. No regeneration or tracker update is required for this client patch.
## Validation and scope
Both reported escape routes passed targeted user gameplay testing. The release contains the accepted native-interaction repair with a version-label update. Native-reference tests cover exact condition validation, idempotence, wrong flags/classes and failed writes; existing routing regressions are also covered. Full release validation is recorded in [testing](https://github.com/Akamarus/Super-Crazy-Rhythm-Castle-Archipelago/blob/v0.29.2/docs/TESTING.md).
Separate investigation confirmed early Violance did not prevent Old Tom's note in the tested post-nectar state, and the Cell Tower Star Eater did not require Cold Storage completion after leaving and returning. Complete prerequisites are not yet isolated, so generation logic remains unchanged.
Intermittent performance stalls, extended-session/multiplayer coverage and remaining native-rule uncertainties remain in [known issues](https://github.com/Akamarus/Super-Crazy-Rhythm-Castle-Archipelago/blob/v0.29.2/docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md). This release does not claim to resolve those reports.
See the [AI disclosure](https://github.com/Akamarus/Super-Crazy-Rhythm-Castle-Archipelago/blob/v0.29.2/docs/AI_DISCLOSURE.md) and [gate acceptance record](https://github.com/Akamarus/Super-Crazy-Rhythm-Castle-Archipelago/blob/v0.29.2/docs/testing/2026-10-22-hub-escape.md).
Release validation: all 45 client regression projects passed, the Release build completed with zero warnings/errors, repository validation passed, and all 10 packaging tests passed. The APWorld asset is reused byte-for-byte from v0.29.1.

entry.title: AEMinecraft v0.7.0rc4
entry.content:
## AEMinecraft v0.7.0-rc.4
**Pre-release.** Fourth test build of v0.7.0. Stay on v0.6.2 if you want a stable game.
This RC only lists what changed since the **[v0.7.0-rc.3 release notes](https://github.com/KuroLynx/AEMinecraft/releases/tag/v0.7.0-rc.3)**. For everything new in v0.7.0, see the **[v0.7.0-rc.1 release notes](https://github.com/KuroLynx/AEMinecraft/releases/tag/v0.7.0-rc.1)**.
### Changed
- **The Biome Finder screen is a map.** Right-clicking the Biome Finder now shows a top-down map of the biomes around you, next to a searchable list of every biome in your dimension. Click a spot on the map or a name in the list to track it. - **An arrow points the way.** While you track a biome, a small arrowhead floats just ahead of your view and turns toward it, like a compass needle. It faces you while you glide, swim or crawl. Its textures live in `textures/misc/biome_finder_arrow/`, so resource packs can replace them. - **Clearing the target.** The biome you're tracking sits at the top of the screen with a ✕ to stop tracking it. Tracking also stops on its own once you walk into that biome.
### Upgrading from rc.3
- **Only the mod jar changed.** Keep the rc.3 apworld and your YAMLs.
